title: Enums and Native Types
description: Define strongly-typed database enums, handle status transitions, and use PostgreSQL custom types safely in TypeScript.

data.text: Enums allow developers to restrict a column's value to a fixed set of predefined options (e.g., order statuses, user roles, billing tiers). In PostgreSQL, Prisma enums map directly to native database `CREATE TYPE ... AS ENUM` statements, providing database-level constraint enforcement and compile-time TypeScript type safety.

data.title: Enum Definition in schema.prisma
data.content: Define enum blocks and reference them as field types in your models.

data.text: When you run `prisma generate`, Prisma exports TypeScript enums directly from `@prisma/client`. You can import and use them in server actions, API routes, and validation schemas (e.g. Zod).

data.title: TypeScript Usage with Zod Validation
Migration Caveat for Enums
data.text: In PostgreSQL, adding a new value to an existing enum (`ALTER TYPE ... ADD VALUE`) is fast and safe. However, removing or renaming enum values in PostgreSQL is non-trivial and often requires creating a new type, migrating columns, and dropping the old type.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Enums enforce valid values at both the database engine and TypeScript compiler levels.
Import enums directly from `@prisma/client` for consistent runtime comparisons.
Plan enum values carefully because renaming or dropping enum values in PostgreSQL requires explicit migration steps.
